extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of political philosophy; readers of Plato's Republic
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and prescriptions for selecting, educating, testing, and provisioning the guardian‑rulers (philosopher‑kings) and diagnostic features of constitutions in Plato's political scheme (Republic Books VII–VIII).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of rulers (natural preference)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rulers should be chosen 'the surest and the bravest, and, if possible, to the fairest; and, having noble and generous tempers, they should also have the natural gifts which will facilitate their education.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference given to those of superior native constitution (courage, steadiness, beauty ideally), combined with dispositions suited to intensive education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural gifts for education
rubrics_metrics.description: Required natural gifts include 'keenness and ready powers of acquisition; a good memory, and be an unwearied solid man who is a lover of labour in any line; or he will never be able to endure the great amount of bodily exercise and ... intellectual discipline and study which we require of him.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These traits are necessary because 'the mind more often faints from the severity of study than from the severity of gymnastics.' Selection should privilege learners with these innate capacities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single‑minded vocation (avoid divided interests)
rubrics_metrics.description: The votary should not have 'a lame or halting industry'—i.e. not be 'half industrious and half idle' nor devoted principally to bodily exercises (gymnastics, hunting) while hating the labour of learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates must show a genuine vocational bent toward philosophical study rather than divided commitments that would undercut sustained intellectual labor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to truth and intellectual shame
rubrics_metrics.description: A suitable soul must not 'hate voluntary falsehood ... but be patient of involuntary falsehood, and ... wallow like a swinish beast in the mire of ignorance, and has no shame at being detected.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection favors those who abhor falsehood and intellectual ignorance alike — moral commitment to truth and intellectual integrity matter, not merely avoidance of deliberate lying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possession of classical virtues
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates should possess temperance, courage, magnificence, and 'every other virtue'—distinguishing true sons (virtuous) from bastards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral and civic virtues are required; deficiencies in parts of virtue imply unfitness to rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early mathematical and scientific training
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculation, geometry and other elements of instruction 'should be presented to the mind in childhood' and serve as preparation for dialectic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce abstract, mathematical disciplines early, but 'not under any notion of forcing our system of education'—education should be made like amusement to reveal natural bent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid compulsion in early learning
rubrics_metrics.description: A freeman ought not to be a slave in the acquisition of knowledge; 'knowledge which is acquired under compulsion obtains no hold on the mind.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pedagogy: present early education as enjoyable rather than coercive so learning takes root voluntarily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialectic as the capstone science
rubrics_metrics.description: Dialectic 'is the coping‑stone of the sciences ... no other science can be placed higher—the nature of knowledge can no further go' — it alone goes directly to first principles and does away with hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dialectic should be taught only after mastery of preparatory sciences (mathematics, harmony, etc.); it is the highest intellectual discipline for grasping the idea of the good.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialectical capacity / comprehension
rubrics_metrics.description: The capacity for such knowledge is 'the great criterion of dialectical talent: the comprehensive mind is always the dialectical'; one must be able to 'give up the use of sight and the other senses' and attain absolute being.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate candidates on ability to abstract, to withstand challenges to received beliefs, and to pursue truth by reason rather than opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age thresholds and educational timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed timeline: selection from the class of twenty‑year‑olds for promotion; at thirty chosen for dialectic testing; a proposed five years of concentrated dialectical study; fifteen years of holding offices/real‑world service; at fifty, those who survive and distinguish themselves attain consummation as rulers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Education is staged: childhood mathematics → adult selection (around 20) → dialectic (around 30) → extended practical experience → final elevation (around 50). Specific durations: five years of dialectic (in text), fifteen years of public service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical service as a test of character
rubrics_metrics.description: After initial dialectical training they 'must be sent down again into the den and compelled to hold any military or other office ... in this way they will get their experience of life ... and there will be an opportunity of trying whether, when they are drawn ... by temptation, they will stand firm or flinch.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Real‑world experience (military/administrative service) is required to prove steadiness and resistance to temptation before final elevation to rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution against early exposure to dialectic (avoid eristic youth)
rubrics_metrics.description: Warns of the danger that youngsters, when they 'first get the taste' of argument, will argue for amusement, imitate refuters, contradict for sport and become lawless — converting philosophy into a bad name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delay dialectic until sufficient maturity to prevent sophistic/eristic habits; manage timing of exposure to reasoning so it fosters truth‑seeking, not argumentative vice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guardians' communal property and subsistence
rubrics_metrics.description: In the perfect State 'no one was to have any of the ordinary possessions of mankind; they were to be warrior athletes and guardians, receiving from the other citizens, in lieu of annual payment, only their maintenance, and they were to take care of themselves and of the whole State.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescribe communal housing, no private property for guardians, and maintenance (not pay) as the economic arrangement to avoid conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender inclusion in guardian training
rubrics_metrics.description: 'You must not suppose that what I have been saying applies to men only and not to women as far as their natures can go.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Women with the requisite natures receive the same education and share in offices as men; selection criteria apply irrespective of sex up to natural limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnostic features of timocracy (government of honour)
rubrics_metrics.description: Timocracy is described by its features: honour given to rulers; abstinence of warrior class from agriculture/handicrafts; common meals; emphasis on gymnastics and military training; fear of admitting philosophers; valorization of military stratagems and perpetual wars; secret longing after gold and silver leading to hoarding, castles and misdirected expenditure; under‑valuation of music.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these behavioral and institutional markers to identify a polity moving away from aristocracy toward timocracy; the passage treats them both as descriptive markers and as evaluative signs of decline.
